sources.title: NGSS MS-ESS2-4: Develop a model to describe the cycling of water through Earth's systems driven by energy from the sun and the force of gravity
Earle, Physical Geology 2nd ed. (BCcampus), 13.1 The Hydrological Cycle
Earle, Physical Geology 2nd ed. (BCcampus), 14.2 Groundwater Flow

note.text: Energy from the sun drives the water cycle up into the sky.

steps.title: Land
steps.instruction: Trace the land, the mountain and the sea floor.

note.text: Gravity pulls water back down: as rain and snow, then downhill over and under the land.
The ocean holds 97% of Earth's water.

steps.title: Snow
steps.instruction: Trace the snow on the mountain top.

note.text: Some water is stored as snow and ice. When it melts in spring, solid water becomes liquid and flows downhill.
Plants pull water up from the soil through their roots.

steps.title: Evaporation
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow rising from the ocean.

note.text: Sunlight warms the ocean, and liquid water evaporates into invisible water vapor, a gas.

steps.title: Transpiration
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow rising from the tree.

note.text: Plants give off water vapor from their leaves. This is called transpiration.
Winds carry the vapor up, where it cools and condenses into tiny droplets or ice crystals: a cloud.

steps.title: Precipitation
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow from the cloud down to the mountain.

note.text: When the droplets or crystals grow heavy, gravity pulls them down as rain or snow.

steps.title: Runoff
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow down the mountain and across to the ocean.

note.text: Water flows downhill in streams and rivers, back to the ocean.

steps.title: Groundwater
steps.instruction: Draw the arrow through the ground to the ocean.

note.text: Some water soaks into the ground and moves slowly through rock and soil. Some of it reaches the ocean.

steps.title: Name the processes
steps.instruction: Pick the name of each numbered process.

targets.role: Water rises from the ocean as vapor.

mistakes.Evaporation: This vapor comes from a plant's leaves, which is called transpiration.

steps.title: What drives it?
steps.question: Which force brings water back down from the clouds and over the land to the sea?

options.feedback: Yes. The sun's energy lifts water up; gravity pulls it back down and downhill.
Sunlight drives evaporation, lifting water up. Gravity pulls it back down.
Wind moves clouds sideways, but gravity makes rain fall and rivers flow downhill.
Magnetism doesn't move water. Gravity does.

steps.title: Changes of state
steps.question: Ocean water evaporates, forms a cloud, and falls as snow on the mountain. What states was it in, in order?

options.text: Liquid, gas, liquid droplets or ice, then solid snow
options.feedback: Right. It evaporated into a gas, condensed into droplets or crystals, and fell as solid snow.
Ocean water starts as a liquid. It becomes a gas when it evaporates.

options.text: It stayed liquid the whole time
options.feedback: Evaporation turns it into a gas, and snow is a solid.
Ocean water is liquid first, then gas, then droplets or ice, then snow.
